I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. That is the system I trust most here. Our county is a main grain area on the North China Plain, and wheat-maize rotation fits the climate, the irrigation conditions, and the way I know how to farm. At my age, I will not spread myself across too many crops. Cotton and vegetables can bring more trouble with labor, management, and market swings. I would rather stay with grain, keep the work familiar, and protect yield.

For wheat, I will use an improved variety, prepare the field with rotary tillage, and keep fertilizer moderate instead of pushing it too hard. Wheat needs the water more here, so I will plan several irrigations through the season. I will watch weeds, aphids, and disease, and I will spray only as needed but I still expect about two pesticide applications in a normal year. For summer maize, I will switch to a hybrid because that is the stronger choice for yield. I will keep fertilizer balanced, rely more on rainfall, and usually give only one irrigation unless the season turns dry. I will keep pest control simple and timely. This way I keep the system steady, the work manageable, and the land in a pattern that suits Quzhou.
